summary: Corrected compute-mamba-ratio guidance and both live cookbook calculators to treat plain speculative intermediate state as separate request-indexed scratch, retain ReplaySSM allocation distinctions, divide request sizing per attention-DP worker, and reserve one usable transient stash slot beyond C*S. Added a focused failing-before/passing-after documentation regression. This changes guidance and calculators only; the reported eight-H100 workload was not rerun.

tests.what_was_measured: Three regression assertions covering separate plain-spec scratch, attention-DP sizing, and the C*S+1 explicit pin; all passed after failing against the recorded base content.
The checked-out MambaSlotAllocator returned None for a transient allocation after all 30 usable slots were held, then succeeded after one slot was freed.
Derived 2.872258 GiB for (6+1)*6 intermediate rows from 2.12 GiB/31 physical state rows; confirmed floor(30/5)=6 and transient demand 31>30; derived DP8 pin boundaries.
No whitespace errors in the delivered patch.

remaining_limitations: The original GLM-5.3-Flash TP8 + attention-DP8 workload on eight H100 GPUs was not rerun.
No GPU execution was used: the deliverable changes repository guidance and JSX sizing arithmetic, and the current allocator boundary was reproduced deterministically on CPU.

The calculators derive model-specific scratch geometry from current source; operators should verify final pool bytes and admitted concurrency from their boot log, especially for tree verification, non-CUDA layouts, or future allocator changes.
ReplaySSM does not use the plain-spec D term: GDN request-indexed ring scratch and KDA per-slot ring bytes remain distinct, and conv rollback scratch can remain.
